page: Microsoft Azure F32as_v7 is an x86_64 architecture server instance belonging to the Fasv7 family. It is powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 processor featuring 32 physical cores and 32 vCPUs running at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB per core. It does not include any local storage or bundled GPUs, though it is Premium Storage capable for external disk attachments.

Benchmark data highlights strong compute capabilities, particularly in single-core tasks. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance and single-threaded gzip compression both rank in the top tier. Multi-core performance via stress-ng and PassMark CPU tests falls into the top 25%, demonstrating robust parallel processing. Memory bandwidth is also highly competitive, with uncached read speeds reaching 215.71 GB/sec and write speeds at 134.66 GB/sec.

This hardware profile is highly cost-efficient for compute-intensive workloads that do not require local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration. The combination of high clock speed and strong database operation benchmarks makes it well-suited for relational databases, web serving, and medium-scale LLM inference. However, the lack of local storage requires relying on network-attached storage, which should be factored into architectural planning.
